summary.text: Apply through the Public Trustee’s Office, or contact CDP directly if the shareholding is $5,000 or below.

details.heading: Value limit for Public Trustee help
details.body: The Public Trustee can help transfer the Deceased’s CDP shares only when the total value of the estate is $50,000 or less.

details.heading: Common documents
details.body: These may include the Death Certificate, Birth Certificate and Marriage Certificate of the Deceased; the beneficiary’s Birth Certificate and Identity Card; and other documents listed by the Public Trustee.

details.heading: If there are other beneficiaries
details.body: Other family members may give up their share, or you may buy over their shares. Only a beneficiary aged 21 or above can give up their share.

details.heading: After you apply
details.body: You will receive an email confirming receipt. A case officer will review the application, and you may be asked for more documents and to pay the administration fee.

steps.name: Check the share value
steps.text: Find out whether the Deceased’s shareholding is $5,000 or below.

steps.name: Choose where to apply
steps.text: If the shareholding is $5,000 or below, approach CDP directly. Otherwise, use the Public Trustee’s Office online application.

steps.name: Prepare your documents
steps.text: Prepare the documents that apply to the Deceased and the beneficiary, such as certificates and identity cards.

steps.name: Send your claim
steps.text: Submit the online application under “Deceased’s estate other than un-nominated CPF moneys / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA”, or approach CDP directly if the shareholding is $5,000 or below.

quotes.text: You will need to submit an online application via https://go.gov.sg/pto under “Deceased’s estate other than un-nominated CPF moneys / Baby Bonus / Edusave / PSEA”.
If the value of the shareholding is $5,000 or below, you can approach CDP directly to claim the Deceased’s shareholding.
Common types of documents required are:
Please take note that the Public Trustee can only assist in the transfer of the Deceased’s CDP shares, if the total value of the estate is $50,000 or less, to the intended transferee.

Death Certificate of Deceased Birth Certificate of Deceased Marriage Certificate of Deceased Decree Nisi Absolute (if the Deceased was divorced) Birth Certificate of Beneficiary Identity Card of Beneficiary

If there are multiple beneficiaries, (e.g., Deceased left behind a spouse and children) the other family members may choose to give up his / her share so claimant can claim the shares. Alternatively, the claimant may buy over the other beneficiary’ shares.
You will get an email confirming your application was received
